Launch applications in a temporary VPN network namespace

Usage: vopono [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  daemon   Run the vopono daemon (requires root)
  exec     Execute an application with the given VPN connection
  list     List running vopono namespaces and applications
  sync     Synchronise local server lists with VPN providers
  servers  List possible server configs for VPN provider, beginning with prefix
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose  Verbose output
      --silent   Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass  read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Run the vopono daemon (requires root)

Usage: vopono daemon [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -v, --verbose  Verbose output
      --silent   Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass  read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -h, --help     Print help

Execute an application with the given VPN connection

Usage: vopono exec [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION>

Arguments:
  <APPLICATION>  Application to run (should be on PATH or full path to binary)

Options:
  -p, --provider <PROVIDER>
          VPN Provider (must be given unless using custom config) [possible values: PrivateInternetAccess, Mullvad, ProtonVPN, MozillaVPN, AzireVPN, AirVPN, IVPN, NordVPN, Warp, Custom, None]
  -v, --verbose
          Verbose output
  -c, --protocol <PROTOCOL>
          VPN Protocol (if not given will use default) [possible values: OpenVpn, Wireguard, AmneziaWG, OpenConnect, OpenFortiVpn, Ssh, Warp, None]
      --silent
          Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass
          read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -i, --interface <INTERFACE>
          Network Interface (if not given, will use first active network interface)
  -s, --server <SERVER>
          VPN Server prefix (must be given unless using custom config)
  -u, --user <USER>
          User with which to run the application (default is current user)
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Group with which to run the application
  -w, --working-directory <WORKING_DIRECTORY>
          Working directory in which to run the application (default is current working directory)
      --custom <CUSTOM>
          Custom VPN Provider - OpenVPN or Wireguard config file (will override other settings)
  -d, --dns <DNS>
          DNS Server (will override provider's DNS server)
      --hosts <HOSTS>
          List of /etc/hosts entries for the network namespace (e.g. "10.0.1.10 webdav.server01.lan","10.0.1.10 vaultwarden.server01.lan"). For a local host you should also provide the open-hosts option
      --open-hosts <OPEN_HOSTS>
          List of hostnames or IP addresses to open on the network namespace (comma separated) hostnames will be resolved locally to IP addresses
      --no-killswitch
          Disable killswitch
  -k, --keep-alive
          Keep-alive - do not close network namespace when launched process terminates
  -o, --open-ports <OPEN_PORTS>
          List of ports to open on network namespace (to allow port forwarding through the tunnel, e.g. for BitTorrent, etc.)
  -f, --forward <FORWARD>
          List of ports to forward from network namespace to host - useful for running servers and daemons
      --no-proxy
          Disable proxying to host machine when forwarding ports
      --firewall <FIREWALL>
          Firewall to use [possible values: IpTables, NfTables]
      --disable-ipv6
          Block all IPv6 traffic
      --postup <POSTUP>
          Path or alias to executable PostUp script or binary for commands to run on the host after bringing up the namespace
      --predown <PREDOWN>
          Path or alias to executable PreDown script or binary for commands to run on the host after before shutting down the namespace
      --vopono-config <VOPONO_CONFIG>
          Path to vopono config TOML file (will be created if it does not exist) Default: ~/.config/vopono/config.toml
      --custom-netns-name <CUSTOM_NETNS_NAME>
          Custom name for the generated network namespace Will use this network namespace directly if it exists
      --allow-host-access
          Allow access to host from network namespace Useful for accessing services on the host locally
      --port-forwarding
          Enable port forwarding for if supported
      --custom-port-forwarding <CUSTOM_PORT_FORWARDING>
          Port forwarding implementation to use for custom config file with --custom-config [possible values: PrivateInternetAccess, Mullvad, ProtonVPN, MozillaVPN, AzireVPN, AirVPN, IVPN, NordVPN, Warp, Custom, None]
      --port-forwarding-callback <PORT_FORWARDING_CALLBACK>
          Path or alias to executable script or binary to be called with the port as an argumnet when the port forwarding is refreshed (PIA only)
      --create-netns-only
          Only create network namespace (does not run application)
      --trojan-host <TROJAN_HOST>
          Trojan server address - hostname or IP, will not verify SSL if IP address is given. Port is optional (default is 443)
      --trojan-password <TROJAN_PASSWORD>
          Trojan server password Set this in ~/.config/vopono/vopono.toml or use --trojan-config to avoid setting this in the command line
      --trojan-no-verify
          Disable SSL verification for Trojan server
      --trojan-config <TROJAN_CONFIG>
          Trojan config file (will override other settings)
      --ssh-proxy-port <SSH_PROXY_PORT>
          Local SOCKS5 port for SSH dynamic forwarding
      --ssh-user <SSH_USER>
          Username for the remote SSH server
      --ssh-port <SSH_PORT>
          Port of the remote SSH server
  -h, --help
          Print help

List running vopono namespaces and applications

Usage: vopono list [OPTIONS] [LIST_TYPE]

Arguments:
  [LIST_TYPE]  VPN Provider [possible values: namespaces, applications]

Options:
  -v, --verbose  Verbose output
      --silent   Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass  read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -h, --help     Print help

Synchronise local server lists with VPN providers

Usage: vopono sync [OPTIONS] [VPN_PROVIDER]

Arguments:
  [VPN_PROVIDER]  VPN Provider - will launch interactive menu if not provided [possible values: PrivateInternetAccess, Mullvad, ProtonVPN, MozillaVPN, AzireVPN, AirVPN, IVPN, NordVPN, Warp, Custom, None]

Options:
  -c, --protocol <PROTOCOL>  VPN Protocol (if not given will try to sync both) [possible values: OpenVpn, Wireguard, AmneziaWG, OpenConnect, OpenFortiVpn, Ssh, Warp, None]
  -v, --verbose              Verbose output
      --silent               Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass              read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -h, --help                 Print help

List possible server configs for VPN provider, beginning with prefix

Usage: vopono servers [OPTIONS] <VPN_PROVIDER>

Arguments:
  <VPN_PROVIDER>  VPN Provider [possible values: PrivateInternetAccess, Mullvad, ProtonVPN, MozillaVPN, AzireVPN, AirVPN, IVPN, NordVPN, Warp, Custom, None]

Options:
  -c, --protocol <PROTOCOL>  VPN Protocol (if not given will list all) [possible values: OpenVpn, Wireguard, AmneziaWG, OpenConnect, OpenFortiVpn, Ssh, Warp, None]
  -v, --verbose              Verbose output
  -s, --prefix <PREFIX>      VPN Server prefix
      --silent               Suppress all output including application output
  -A, --askpass              read sudo password from program specified in SUDO_ASKPASS environment variable
  -h, --help                 Print help
